title: Social Responsibilities of Business and Business Ethics

learn.hook: A company may follow every law and still pollute a river right up to the legal limit. Is that enough? Social responsibility asks business to do more than the law demands.
points: Social responsibility of business is its obligation to make decisions and take actions that are desirable in terms of the objectives and values of society.

Legal responsibility means obeying laws: it is compulsory and enforced by the state. Social responsibility is broader and largely voluntary: it includes legal duties plus actions that benefit society beyond what the law requires.
A socially responsible business looks at the effect of its decisions on owners, workers, consumers, the government, the community and the environment, not just on profit.

In India, Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 requires certain large companies to spend a part of their profits on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities, making some social spending a legal duty for them.

example.q: A cement company pays its taxes, follows pollution norms and also, on its own, runs a free school and plants trees near its plant. Which actions are legal responsibility and which go beyond it?
steps: Paying taxes and following pollution norms are required by law: legal responsibility.
Running a free school and planting trees are voluntary actions that benefit society beyond the law.
Social responsibility includes both, but is wider than legal responsibility.
example.answer: Taxes and pollution norms: legal responsibility; free school and tree planting: social responsibility beyond the law.

learn.reallife: Many Indian companies run CSR projects in sanitation, education and health in villages around their plants.

learn.hook: Why should a profit-making company care about the village next to its factory? Because, in the long run, its own survival depends on it.
points: Justification for existence and growth: business exists to serve society; its long-run growth depends on providing goods and services that society values.

Long-term interest of the firm: a good public image built through social responsibility helps the firm in the long run. Avoidance of government regulation: voluntary responsible behaviour reduces the need for strict government rules.

Maintenance of society: if business ignores society, people may react with protests; responsible behaviour helps maintain peace and order. Availability of resources with business: business has finance and talent that can be used to solve social problems.

Converting problems into opportunities: business can turn social problems into profitable opportunities (e.g. cleaner technology, waste recycling). Better environment for doing business: a society with fewer problems gives better conditions for business.
Holding business responsible for social problems: business has often caused or added to problems like pollution, so it should help solve them.

example.q: A paper mill that polluted a river now treats its waste water and also sells recycled paper made from waste. Which arguments for social responsibility does this reflect?
steps: The mill contributed to pollution, so it takes responsibility for the problem.
Selling recycled paper turns a waste problem into a business opportunity.
example.answer: Holding business responsible for social problems, and converting problems into opportunities.

learn.reallife: Some Indian companies have turned waste plastic into roads and furniture: converting a social problem into a business opportunity.

topics.title: The case against social responsibility, and the reality

learn.hook: Some economists argue that a business does its job best by maximising profit and leaving social work to the government. Do they have a point?
points: Violation of profit-maximisation objective: critics say the only responsibility of business is to maximise profits; SR goes against this.
Burden on consumers: the cost of social programmes may be passed on to consumers through higher prices.
Lack of social skills: business managers are trained in business, not in solving social problems, which should be left to specialised agencies.
Lack of broad public support: the public generally does not like business getting involved in social programmes, so it is hard to run them successfully.

Reality: forces that have made business more socially responsive include threat of public regulation, pressure of labour movement, impact of consumer consciousness, development of social standards, development of business education, the link between social interest and business interest, and development of a professional managerial class.

example.q: A critic says: 'A toy maker spending on village schools will raise toy prices and its managers know nothing about teaching.' Which two arguments against SR is he making?
steps: Higher prices passed to buyers = burden on consumers.
Managers lacking expertise in education = lack of social skills.
example.answer: Burden on consumers and lack of social skills.

learn.reallife: Growing consumer awareness in India, through consumer forums and social media reviews, pushes firms to act more responsibly.

learn.hook: Making good products, obeying the law, not hurting religious sentiments in ads and donating to flood relief: four very different kinds of responsibility.
points: Economic responsibility: as an economic institution, business must produce goods and services that society wants and sell them at a profit.
Legal responsibility: every business must obey the laws of the land; a law-abiding firm is a socially responsible one.
Ethical responsibility: behaviour that society expects but which is not written into law, e.g. respecting religious sentiments and dignity of people while advertising.
Discretionary responsibility: purely voluntary obligations that a firm takes on, e.g. donating to charity, supporting educational institutions or helping flood victims.

In case questions, look for clues: 'produce what society wants at a profit' → economic; 'comply with law' → legal; 'not required by law, but expected' → ethical; 'voluntary donation or charity' → discretionary.

example.q: A detergent company withdraws an ad that could hurt a community's religious feelings, though no law required this. Which kind of responsibility is this?
steps: No law required it, so it is not legal responsibility.
It is behaviour society expects, respecting sentiments.
That is ethical responsibility.

learn.reallife: During floods in Assam and Kerala, many companies donated relief material and money on their own: discretionary responsibility.

learn.hook: Shareholders want returns, workers want fair pay, customers want quality and the town wants clean air. A responsible business balances all of them.
points: Towards shareholders/owners: provide a fair and regular return on investment; ensure safety of investment; give regular, accurate and full information about the company's working.
Towards workers: provide opportunity for meaningful work; good working conditions; fair wages; democratic leadership; respect for workers' right to form unions; welfare facilities.

Towards consumers: supply goods of the right quality at reasonable prices; avoid adulteration, poor quality and misleading or dishonest advertising; provide after-sales service; inform consumers about the product; ensure safety.
Towards the government and community: respect the law and pay taxes honestly; behave as a good citizen; protect the natural environment; help weaker and backward sections; respect social values.

example.q: A company (a) declares a fair dividend, (b) installs safety guards on machines, (c) stops adding cheap filler to its spices, and (d) pays taxes honestly. Match each to the interest group.
steps: (a) Dividend = responsibility to shareholders.
(b) Machine safety = responsibility to workers.
(c) No adulteration = responsibility to consumers.
(d) Honest taxes = responsibility to the government.

learn.reallife: Consumer commissions under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 hear complaints when firms fail in their responsibility towards consumers.

learn.hook: The smog over north Indian cities every winter and foam on some rivers are reminders that business activity can harm the environment.
points: Environment means the totality of man's surroundings, both natural and man-made. Pollution is the addition of harmful substances that damage it.

Causes of pollution by business: air pollution (smoke and gases from factories and vehicles, e.g. carbon monoxide); water pollution (chemicals and waste dumped into rivers and lakes); land pollution (dumping of toxic and industrial waste on land, reducing its quality); noise pollution (factories and vehicles, causing stress, hearing problems and other health issues).

Need for pollution control: reduction of health hazards; reduced risk of liability (firms may have to pay damages to victims); cost savings (efficient processes cut waste); improved public image; other social benefits (clearer visibility, cleaner buildings, better quality of life and natural resources).

Role of business: definite commitment by top management; ensuring the commitment is shared by all employees; clear policies for good raw materials, clean technology and scientific waste disposal; complying with laws; participating in government programmes (e.g. cleaning rivers, tree plantation); periodic assessment of pollution control programmes; educational workshops and training.

example.q: A dyeing unit in Tiruppur discharges coloured waste water into a river. Name the type of pollution, one health or legal risk to the firm, and one step it can take.
steps: Waste into a river = water pollution.
Risk: health hazards for people downstream and liability to pay damages.
Step: install effluent treatment and adopt cleaner technology.
example.answer: Water pollution; health hazard and liability risk; treat effluent and use clean technology.

learn.reallife: Under the Namami Gange programme, industries along the Ganga are required to treat their waste water, and many businesses take part in cleanup drives.

learn.hook: A salesman could earn a bigger bonus by hiding a product defect. Nothing stops him except ethics.
points: Business ethics refers to the socially determined moral principles and standards that should govern business activities; they guide what is right and wrong in business conduct.
Ethics and social responsibility are linked: ethical behaviour (honesty, fairness, not cheating) is the base of responsible business.

Elements of business ethics: top management commitment (leaders must set the example); publication of a 'code' (a written code of ethics covering fundamental honesty, adherence to laws, product safety and quality, workplace health and safety, conflicts of interest, employment practices, marketing practices, financial reporting, etc.).

Establishment of compliance mechanisms (e.g. careful recruitment, training, reporting systems for violations, audits); involving employees at all levels (employees at every level implement ethics, so they must be involved); measuring results (regularly checking how well ethical standards are followed).

example.q: A company prints a code of conduct, but its CEO regularly ignores it, and no one checks whether it is followed. Which elements of business ethics are missing?
steps: The CEO ignoring the code = no top management commitment.
No checking = no compliance mechanism and no measuring of results.
A code alone is not enough.
example.answer: Top management commitment, compliance mechanisms and measuring results are missing.

learn.reallife: Many Indian companies have whistle-blower policies that let employees report unethical acts safely: a compliance mechanism in action.
